clue.text: Pack with some cards for ship's labourer

parts.note: a pack of cards is a deck
the cards a player holds are a hand

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles a pack, keeping a handful of cards aside for a sailor's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a crew member doing manual work on a vessel's deck, a ship's labourer.

parts.note: suggests a sharp-featured person, but means a number written with a point in it, such as 2.5

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointed' suggests sharp features; here it means having a decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: A number such as 3.14 contains a point separating whole units from fractions, so it is literally a figure with a point.

definitions.meaning: behaving like a cat, which unsheathes its claws; the question mark flags the playful sense

explanation.surface: Someone turns nasty, showing their claws in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A catty remark is spiteful, and something like a cat is one that shows its claws.

clue.text: Difficult joint? By the way it is!

parts.note: difficult means hard
the shoulder is a body joint

explanation.surface: A tricky joint, mentioned in passing with a casual 'by the way'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as a conversational aside, but means beside the road. A HARD SHOULDER is the emergency lane at the side of a British motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The emergency strip running alongside a motorway lies literally beside the roadway.

clue.text: Found in tin, a chocolate chip

indicators.note: says the letters are found inside the following words, run together

explanation.surface: A chocolate chip turns up inside a biscuit tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip served with toppings in Mexican-style snacks is this food.

definitions.meaning: a small error, as in a ... of the tongue

explanation.surface: Wearing the petticoat was an error.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a woman's underskirt and a minor blunder.

clue.text: Flier allowed to follow flea all over the place

indicators.note: puts the word for allowed after the jumbled flea
scattered everywhere, so the letters of flea are mixed up

parts.note: allowed means let

explanation.surface: A flea, permitted to roam, jumps in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aviator or a jumping flea, but it is a handout; 'all over the place' jumbles the flea and 'to follow' puts the word for allowed last.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a printed handout distributed to the public, the same thing as this pamphlet.

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: emptying the word tray removes its insides, keeping only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise to find the pastry tray bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' looks like an exclamation, but is the definition in its sense of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion and virtue, a form of moral goodness.

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin
jams means gets stuck, sticks

explanation.surface: A frustrated musician curses when the instrument seizes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, as when someone says 'drat' or 'bother'.

clue.text: Crate ordered to provide for event?

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters of crate are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A crate is ordered in to supply a function.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food and drink at a party or function is to do the catering for it.

clue.text: Greek character with stick — that's bendy

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a walking stick is a cane

explanation.surface: A Greek man has a bendy walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicane is a sharp double bend added to a racetrack or road, so it is a bendy section.

explanation.surface: Some blossom appears during the spring season.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a spring month and the hawthorn's white flower.

clue.text: Maintaining power, lord's way disrupted fencing

indicators.note: holding something within, so the jumbled letters keep the power letter inside
thrown into disorder, so the letters of lord's way are rearranged

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A lord keeps his authority while a fence blocks his path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges LORDSWAY into SWORDLAY, and 'Maintaining' places P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing is the sport of combat with blades, which is swordplay.

parts.note: one circuit of a track is a lap
best means top, as in top marks

explanation.surface: The best circuit board for a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal machine that rests on one's knees is a kind of computer.

indicators.note: rigged or altered, so the letters of Gestapo are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Nazi secret police set a delivery fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee paid for sending mail by post.

explanation.surface: A gambler has been cured of his habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who wagers and someone recovered from illness.

indicators.note: taking someone in, so the word for minister holds the a

parts.note: a rector is a clergyman, a minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman welcomes a nuclear device to the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the apparatus in which a controlled nuclear chain reaction takes place.

indicators.note: written again in a new form, so the letters of novel isn't are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's rewritten book is not ruined after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to pay one's debts means being bankrupt, financially ruined.

clue.text: Something introduced yours truly sent off

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves, I

indicators.note: gone wrong, so the letters of sent are rearranged

explanation.surface: The writer posted off something by way of introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' is the letter-writer's sign-off, standing for the writer, I; 'off' signals the jumble of the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece inserted into a page, garment or map, something put in.

definitions.meaning: an officer in certain churches, such as Presbyterian ones
a small tree bearing dark berries

explanation.surface: A tree belonging to the church's officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lay church officer and the tree with elderflowers and berries.

indicators.note: leaving behind, so the word for popular drops out

parts.note: Spain is a nation
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A country leaves behind its favourite holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa town with mineral springs is a health resort.

clue.text: Hindu teacher moved across the Ganges perhaps before one

indicators.note: puts the word for crossing the river ahead of the one

parts.note: crossing a river such as the Ganges by swimming, so swam
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Hindu teacher swims across the holy river ahead of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Plant we see, a new daffodil initially

indicators.note: made new, so the letters of we see a are rearranged
takes the first letter of daffodil

explanation.surface: We see a fresh daffodil in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges WESEEA into SEAWEE, and 'initially' adds D from daffodil.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is marine algae, loosely counted as a plant growing in the sea.

definitions.meaning: a vessel, one example of any boat or aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to build a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for making by hand and a noun for any vessel.

clue.text: By the sound of it, movement of water secured

indicators.note: says a word for the moving sea is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the rise and fall of the sea is the tide

explanation.surface: Something fastened against the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied is fastened with rope or string, held secure.

clue.text: Livelier person going downhill at the end of the working week?

parts.words: the end of the working week
parts.note: Friday ends the working week; Fri is its abbreviation
a skier descends a slope

explanation.surface: A skier heads for the slopes on Friday, full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and full of energy, so the comparative means livelier.
